content:
The image shows a single mango leaf laid on a white background. Key observations:

- The leaf is mostly green but has a dark, blackish-brown superficial coating/discoloration covering large portions of the upper surface
- The dark patches appear as a surface layer — not sunken lesions, not raised spots, not powdery
- The dark material looks like a coating sitting on top of the leaf tissue, concentrated along mid-vein areas and spreading across the blade
- No galls, no powdery white growth, no angular bacterial spots, no curling/crumpling, no necrotic margins
- The pattern is consistent with a superficial fungal growth on honeydew deposits

This matches **Sooty Mould** — superficial dark mycelium forming black encrustation on leaf surfaces, not penetrating tissue, growing on sugary secretions from sap-feeding insects.

The coating is not sunken (ruling out anthracnose), not powdery white (ruling out powdery mildew), not angular raised spots (ruling out bacterial canker), and there are no galls, weevil damage, or dieback symptoms."}
